summaryRaw: Design Everything to see here. Introducing MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. Featuring a groundbreaking tandem OLED display with Touch, Dynamic Island, a redesigned thermal system, an enhanced audio system, and slimmer display borders — all in a lighter design. It’s the pinnacle of pro. PROLED XDR Brilliance within reach. PROLED XDR combines breakthrough tandem OLED technology with advanced algorithms in the display engine, delivering Extreme Dynamic Range and stunning visual fidelity for the ultimate front-of-screen performance. As a reference-caliber display, it delivers outstanding precision for filmmaking, design, and even medical imaging.6 With unparalleled brightness and contrast, deeper blacks, and an exceptionally wide color gamut, you’ll immediately see why it’s the world’s best laptop display. Strength in numbers. Up to1000 nitssustained full-screen brightness4 Up to2000 nitspeak HDR and SDR brightness 10,000,000:1contrast ratio True Tonetechnology P3 + Adobe RGBwide color ProMotionadaptive 10–120Hz refresh rate Touch Magic on tap. Thoughtfully designed for Mac, Touch introduces a whole new way to interact with your work. The Touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so you feel like you’re touching the content itself. Everyday experiences like scrolling and pinching to zoom feel natural and responsive. And new, intuitive interactions let you do even more, like manipulating 3D objects or playing virtual instruments. Scroll. Move through content by sliding your finger across it. Zoom. Pinch to zoom in on photos, documents, web pages, and more. Draw. Sketch and annotate directly onscreen. Dynamic Island Top of screen.Top of mind. Dynamic Island is the new home for Spotlight and Live Activities.7,8 Just like on iPhone, it’s a quick way to see and interact with important information. You can search your Mac, ask a question, track an activity, or control your music — all in one easy‑to‑reach place. Adobe After Effects Spotlight Quickly find what you’re looking for on your Mac — including documents, images, contacts, and emails. You can also open apps, send a message, or see your Clipboard history.7 Adobe Acrobat Live Activities Get real-time updates at a glance. Pick up a call, accept an AirDrop request, track your food delivery, or pause a song with a tap of your finger.8 Siri AI Siri AI is your conversational AI assistant with entirely new capabilities.7 Ask open-ended questions, brainstorm ideas for work or creative projects, and engage in natural, back‑and‑forth conversations. Siri AI is available in English. Usage limits may apply. Performance M5 Pro. M5 Max. Power players. Our most powerful chips ever built for a pro laptop. Both M5 Pro and M5 Max deliver phenomenal single- and multithreaded CPU performance and faster unified memory — giving you the kind of speed you’ve never thought possible. With a powerful Neural Accelerator built into each GPU core, you can fly through AI tasks at mind-bending speeds. Storage is up to twice as fast9 and configurable up to 16TB. And it’s all backed by a redesigned thermal architecture. Houdini Houdini Run graphics-intensive workflows with responsiveness that keeps up with your imagination. The M5 Pro and M5 Max chips each feature a GPU with enhanced shader cores and a third-generation ray-tracing engine, so 3D modeling is crisper and clearer than ever. And Dynamic Caching optimizes on-chip memory to significantly increase GPU utilization — providing a performance boost for apps like Blender, Unity Editor, and AAA games. Nuke by Foundry M5 Pro M5 Pro delivers game-changing power for scientists, engineers, software developers, and creative pros tackling intensive projects. Up to 10.9x faster than M1 Pro10 Maxon Cinema 4D M5 Max Our most powerful chip ever built for a pro laptop. M5 Max is perfect for 3D VFX artists, AI developers, and film composers. Up to 12x faster than M1 Max11 AI State‑of-the‑artificial intelligence. Apple silicon, and every major subsystem that powers it, is designed for AI — creating a platform that comprehensively unites hardware, software, and ecosystem. So you can run demanding on-device AI workloads with incredible power efficiency. And as always, security and privacy are designed in, not just bolted on. LM Studio, TouchDesigner Use AI to streamline workflows, create agents, manage inventory, or analyze code. Locally run advanced AI apps like Comfy Desktop for image generation, Msty Studio and LM Studio for running LLMs, and Topaz Video for video enhancement. And with AI built into the apps you already use, like Logic Pro and Adobe Photoshop, you can split audio into stems or make complex image modifications in seconds. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.More personal. More powerful. The next generation of Apple Intelligence is centered around you, integrated into your apps, and built with privacy. Apple Intelligence powers Siri AI — an entirely new version of Siri that’s more personal, conversational, and powerful, along with helpful features across apps.7 Siri AI is available in English. Usage limits may apply. Great powers come with great privacy. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI are designed to protect your privacy at every step. With powerful on-device processing, Apple Intelligence is aware of your personal information without collecting your personal information. And with groundbreaking Private Cloud Compute, Apple Intelligence can draw on larger server-based models, without making your data accessible to Apple or anyone else. Battery Up to 24 hours of battery life. Go from dawn to done. MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display delivers up to 24 hours of battery life,1 and both models provide the same great performance whether they’re plugged in or on battery. Which means you get to spend more time thinking about outlets for your passion, not your laptop. Up to13 more hoursthan Intel-based MacBook Pro1 Fast charge up to50% batteryin 30 minutes34 Pro Workflows Super. Natural. Whether you’re a designer or a coder, the combination of incredible processing power and advanced display capabilities will work wonders for your workflow. The display offers calibration and industry-standard reference modes for filmmakers, photographers, and graphic designers. And macOS makes the most of the graphics, memory, and machine learning capabilities of Apple silicon, so your apps perform their best. Draw Things AI Born to run. Mac is optimized to handle the world’s most advanced AI apps. Run image generation apps like Comfy Desktop and Draw Things, LLM apps like Msty Studio and LM Studio, and video enhancement apps like Topaz Video. Xcode Coding Get with the program. Run virtual machines and develop code across the stack. Use AI tools to help you build apps, save time with predictive code completion, and test iOS software directly onscreen with Touch in Xcode. Use tools like Unity Editor, Create ML, TensorFlow, PyTorch, NAG Fortran Compiler, Docker, IntelliJ IDEA, and more. Adobe Photoshop Photoediting Handle large image files, no sweat. Edit and retouch photos whether in the studio or on location with apps like Adobe Lightroom, Adobe Photoshop, Capture One, Pixelmator Pro, Topaz Photo, DxO PhotoLab 10, and more. DaVinci Resolve Studio Video Cut to the chase. Fly through 8K footage and tackle motion graphics and compositing with superfast render times. For virtual productions, genlock35 keeps cameras and displays perfectly synchronized for real-time visual rendering. Create your masterpiece with tools like DaVinci Resolve Studio, Adobe Premiere, Final Cut Pro, Motion, Adobe After Effects, Nuke by Foundry, and more. JupyterLab, Microsoft PowerPoint, Terminal Business Multitask like a boss. Create documents and presentations and collaborate across apps and video conferences — and do it all at once. Keep business moving with Microsoft 365, Claude, Slack, Zoom, Figma, Keynote, and more. MATLAB STEM Make Mac your lab partner. Run complex simulations or DNA sequencing or analyze large datasets in any STEM environment. Use tools like MATLAB, NASA TetrUSS, Oxford Nanopore MinKNOW, Falcon MD, Shapr3D, SurgicalAR, Vectorworks, Archicad, and more. Maxon Cinema 4D 3D animationand design Bring your imagination to life. Build intricate texturing in 3D artwork and use gestures to manipulate objects directly onscreen in Blender with Touch. Create complex animations and render high-resolution scenes with Maxon Cinema 4D, Maxon Redshift, Autodesk Maya, Adobe Substance Painter, Houdini, and more. Avid Pro Tools Musicproduction Produce the whole album. Compose, record, and mix across thousands of tracks with hundreds of plug-ins in real time. And use Touch to control faders and instruments directly in Logic Pro. Make it all happen with apps like Logic Pro, Avid Pro Tools, Ableton Live, Cubase, Adobe Audition, FL Studio, MainStage, and more. Falcon MD Medicalimaging The picture of health. With new DICOM medical imaging reference modes, the PROLED XDR display can be used to review medical images with outstanding grayscale accuracy and contrast when used for non-diagnostic reviews, research, and educational purposes.6 And it can easily be switched back to a default preset for general use. CONTROL Resonant Gaming Play favorites. Enjoy immersive gaming thanks to the exceptional graphics capabilities, PROLED XDR display, ProMotion, and six-speaker sound system with Spatial Audio. Turn on Game Mode for smoother frame rates. And play titles like CONTROL Resonant, Valheim, Crimson Desert Enhanced, Palworld, Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate, and more. Audio and Camera The best audio system in a laptop. Mic drop. Redesigned woofers and tweeters coupled with a high-quality camera and advanced mics ensure that you’ll look and sound like a pro — even when you’re on the go. Audio More boom to fill the room. Six speakers with an all-new woofer design deliver 50 percent deeper bass. Updated tweeters shape sound dispersion for remarkable clarity. Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos wrap you in immersive sound for music and movies. And a studio-quality three-mic array with Voice Isolation keeps your voice crisp and clear, even in a noisy room. Camera You, always in view. The 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View keeps you in frame during video calls, even as you move or when more people join your frame. And advanced video stabilization lets you touch the screen without causing your camera feed to shake. Ports and Connectivity Plug in. Go all out. With a versatile array of ports, MacBook Pro is built for a wide range of workflows. Models with M5 Pro support up to three external displays over a single Thunderbolt 5 port, and models with M5 Max support up to four. So you can build a workspace that works the way you need it to. And the Apple-designed N1 wireless chip supports Wi‑Fi 73 and Bluetooth 6 for seamless connectivity. MagSafe 3 HDMI Headphone jack 3x Thunderbolt 5 SDXC Up to 4 external displays Security No compromises. Security starts with Apple silicon and extends to the macOS architecture. This deep integration of hardware and software, along with automatic updates and built-in antivirus protection, helps keep MacBook Pro stable and secure for the long term. At the heart of MacBook Pro is the Secure Enclave, a dedicated security subsystem that’s separate from the main processor. It keeps your most sensitive data, including encryption keys and biometric information, fully isolated from the rest of the system — the same protection that powers Touch ID and Find My. comments.author: CountSessine
comments.textRawHtml:
Touch-screen Macs is kind of a terrible development for anyone who loves the Mac. It's not just a harmless feature that you can ignore if you don't want it, because it's customer-facing and will now generate complaints and bugs from people who do use it. Those people will complain (rightly) that macOS UI widgets are too small to accurately manipulate with your fingers (they are indeed too small) and don't make sense with a touch screen (they don't make sense).

That means Apple will begin imposing all sorts of UI dreck on all of us, whether we want to use our screens as touch surfaces or not.

This is basically what happened with Microsoft - Windows Vista and 7 were installed in plenty of laptops with touchscreens, and customers would complain about not being able to maximize windows without closing them, not being able to open menus without touching toolbar buttons, etc.

Eventually Microsoft listened to them and we got Windows 8. Now this is the beginning of the same process for macOS.

children.author: Grombobulous
children.textRawHtml:
I would argue that once the dust settled post-Windows 8 with Windows 10 a full decade ago, the touch screen has been the opposite of what you’ve described for Windows systems. It absolutely is a harmless feature that you can ignore. There’s no reason not to have one.

Same goes for Linux. My CachyOS install on my Framework 13 Pro has a touch screen. There’s literally no downside for me having it. I don’t have to use it if I don’t want to. But if I want to scroll a website or scrub a video the option is there.

children.author: tannhaeuser
children.textRawHtml: I don't think you can say that. Windows 10+ has a tablet mode that is completely detached from desktop mode, and it's a global toggle. Switching on tablet mode brings full-screen, upscaled, simplified explorer and settings, and switches off the classic desktop launcher with paper bin, shortcuts, etc. in favor of a larger "Start"-type menu launcher. What deeper and experimental integration there was in Windows 8 had just been removed as it became clear MS couldn't quite sell into the iPad/Android tablet market or compete in terms of power management. After stripping most of Windows 8 innovations, what remains is a touch keyboard, touch mouse emulation, and a few affordances in explorer to make tablets not outright terrible, with the target audience education and mbas interested in mobile powerpoint and web/mail.

children.textRawHtml:
The introduction of the mouse led to developers paying less attention to keyboard shortcuts and function keys, but I don’t see anyone seriously saying computers should not have mice.

Or for that matter, that adding support for game controllers (something that has actually happened with Linux desktops) would led to curtailed development of non-controller parts.

children.author: jasomill
children.textRawHtml:
I've never hard particularly good experiences with using Windows laptops as tablets, but mostly on account of form factor rather than software.

The sweet spot for me is the iPad mini, but I tend to use tablets as glorified e-readers and video players; the only serious work I do on them is reading.

With that said, I have zero problem with touchscreens or convertable form factors. In fact, I used a Surface Pro for years as my main laptop, and it was one of the best Windows laptops I've used.

But again, I'm not a big fan of mobile devices as primary computing devices unless I'm actually working on the go.

Even for commuting back and forth between an office and a home office, I'd rather just put something along the lines of a Mac Studio in a bag — for a few months last year, it was actually a SFF (not micro, weighed about 10 kg) Dell OptiPlex in an aluminium briefcase, which was fine!

With that said, I have zero problem with touchscreens or convertable form factors. In fact, I used a Surface Pro for years as my main laptop, and it was one of the best Windows laptops I've used.

But again, I'm not a big fan of mobile devices as primary computing devices unless I'm actually working on the go.

Even for commuting back and forth between an office and a home office, I'd rather just put something along the lines of a Mac Studio in a bag — for a few months last year, it was actually a SFF (not micro, weighed about 10 kg) Dell OptiPlex in an aluminium briefcase, which was fine!

children.author: Grombobulous
children.textRawHtml:
But even an half-way experience is an improvement for a feature that costs nearly zero dollars to include.

One of the most common actions among all computer users, zooming and centering a photo, is easier with a touch screen.

Even adding just that one thing is worth having a touch screen for.

Another example: working in the iOS simulator is now way easier because you can touch your apps that you're developing for iOS and iPadOS. And, by the way, macOS can run iOS/iPadOS apps directly from the App Store, so if there's something you really want to run that you just can't find a macOS equivalent for, there you go, you can just do it and interact with the app more naturally.

The only touchscreen laptop I ever understood the appeal of was that one Lenovo one where you can fold the bottom back to make it a literal tablet or prop up as a kickstand.

The value of “tablet mode” would mainly be if I want to do content consumption, like watch video or read a book, while on the couch or in bed since it allows a wider range of postures you can sit or lay in when you don’t have to rest it on a flat surface.

If you can’t fold it back I just don’t get the appeal.

children.author: freehorse
children.textRawHtml:
"Tablet mode" was not necessary to use for touchscreen, though. As far as I remember you can have full touchscreen functionality in the default mode of windows. I had a surface pro 4 for some years and I do not remember using tablet mode ever.

Windows 8, which was tablet-oriented, was one of these skip generations of windows that nobody cares about in the end, and when the next comes everybody forgets. I never installed it anyway. I have not owned a touchscreen laptop myself since then, but from friends that have and I have used theirs, it is like OP described as a "harmless additional feature/why not", something that just makes certain interactions a bit faster.

But especially on an actual laptop, one that you cannot just separate the screen from the keyboard, stuff like "virtual keyboard" and "tablet mode" matter much less because it is not like you will take it and use it as a pure tablet anyway.

children.author: CountSessine
children.textRawHtml:
I made this point below, but Windows 10 still doesn't have the display-real-estate efficiency of Windows 7. Windows 10 wastes all kind of screen space on large, flat surfaces that a non-touch-screen user will never use. Windows 7 wasn't as pretty as Windows 10, but it was better at displaying information.

So actually, you are harmed by this decision every day you use a Windows 10/11 laptop. You live with this every day. You just don't know what you're missing.

children.author: Grombobulous
children.textRawHtml:
Windows 10/11 looks almost identical to Windows 7. I really don’t see a major difference.

But even if I accept your premise, I’ll remind you that Windows 7 came out 19 years ago. I didn’t exactly own a 27” 4K monitor in 2009, and a 14” or 16” screen laptop in 2009 would not have been thin and light like it is today. 2009 was like “my bezels are over a half inch wide” era.

The OS is fully scalable as well. You can just make it smaller in a very granular way. Windows 7 wasn’t capable of that.
